title: One step of the guessing phase
statement: Let $M$ be a finite deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary input, let $d$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, let $u$ be a binary word, and let $b$ be a bit. One step of the guessing-phase machine for $M$ under choice bit $b$, from the invariant configuration corresponding to $(d,u)$, equals the invariant configuration corresponding to the one-step successor of $d$ and the word obtained by appending $b$ to $u$ if $M$ emits an output symbol from $d$, and otherwise leaving $u$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
replaced: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine over the binary alphabet, $d$ one of its configurations, $u$ a captured word and $b$ a choice bit. One nondeterministic step of the guessing-phase machine of $M$ under $b$ maps the invariant configuration for $(d, u)$ to the invariant configuration for the stepped configuration of $M$, with $b$ appended to the captured word exactly when $M$ emits an output symbol at $d$.
